goal: Publish agy 1.1.3 compatibility evidence and the completed two-profile real CLI integration.
completed: Detected that the installed client had changed to agy 1.1.3 and confirmed the existing version gate failed closed.
Revalidated two distinct identities, concurrent execution, forced refresh, clean-third non-reuse, and cleanup under agy 1.1.3.
Added a separate 1.1.3 compatibility entry and evidence document.
Updated provider, doctor, and experimental CLI version gates for 1.1.3.
Completed the real experimental import and concurrent exec journey for both accounts with distinct managed credentials.
Added a regression check that rejects execution when the installed client differs from the profile capture version.
The complete local gate passes with 62 automated tests.
nextActions: Review and merge the agy 1.1.3 compatibility and real CLI integration pull request.
decisions: Direct refresh-token injection is a viable version-scoped agy 1.1.2 and 1.1.3 Linux SSH profile mechanism; the official client continues to own refresh and backend requests.
Profile execution requires the installed client version to equal the version recorded when the profile was imported.
Real operator-controlled state may be inspected temporarily during authorized research, but independent OAuth enrollment remains gated by product-scope and ADR approval.
openQuestions: Does Google rotate the refresh token during long-lived use, and can agy-auth capture that update atomically per profile?
What at-rest protection should project-owned refresh credentials use?

notRun: Rollback journal under injected faults and client versions beyond 1.1.3 were not run.

risks: The contract is reverse engineered and version-specific; refresh credentials are bearer secrets and require protected storage.
doNotRepeat: Do not copy live access tokens; the minimal refresh-token envelope is sufficient.
Do not enable production switching from single-account evidence.
